Title: First, Make Me Care
Excerpt: Writing advice: some nonfiction fails because it opens with background instead of a hook. Find the single anomaly that makes the topic interesting and lead with that.
Text:
> "Venice built a maritime empire from a city that couldn't feed itself; so who fed it?"

That sentence creates a question you want answered, and you keep reading. Most
nonfiction introductions do not do that — they start with background.

When writing, first, make the reader care. See the [maritime empire of *Venice*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stato_da_M%C3%A0r)
for the example, and the [notes](/notes/hooks) for the rest.
